name: Harshavardhan Kuthadi
headline: Software engineer building web and mobile apps, backend services, and data pipelines.

about.intro: I like figuring out how things work, building my own version, and sticking with a problem until it makes sense.
paragraphs: I studied electronics before moving into software. My interests still span hardware, machine learning, and computing on devices. I like the point where code starts doing something you can see or interact with.
I enjoy taking a problem apart, trying things, and debugging until I understand what's going on. Building a small project is usually how I get to grips with a new idea.

I also like building with other people: talking through an approach, hearing a different take, and taking responsibility for getting my part working. That mix of learning, experimenting, and working things out is what I enjoy about engineering.

experience.summary: I've been a Product Engineer at Pretorin since May 2026. I work across the web app, backend, and agent tools. My current work includes Compliance Claw, a customer-deployable product that connects OpenClaw with Pretorin and runs as an always-on compliance agent.
highlights: Own development of Compliance Claw and the in-app assistant that helps people navigate Pretorin and get support.
Work on MCP hosting and plugins so people can use Pretorin's tools from OpenAI, Anthropic, and other AI clients.
Build Python and FastAPI services that check permissions, look up relevant evidence, and keep responses linked to their sources. Add tests for denied access and prompt injection.
Improve the agent development stack and CLI releases. Added signed packages, checksums, and software bills of materials; reduced macOS installation time from seven minutes to three.
experience.overview: Compliance Claw, the in-app assistant, and integrations with AI clients.

experience.summary: I co-founded TappedIn and built its React Native app and PostgreSQL backend. People use virtual currency to back emerging artists and track how their picks grow. The app is live on the App Store with over 1,000 users.
highlights: Built artist discovery, user portfolios, trading, and account flows with React Native and Expo.
Keep balance changes and trades in a single database transaction, with checks that prevent a repeated request from charging twice.
Batch Spotify artist updates through a queue and retry failed requests. Added tests for the app, APIs, database permissions, and trading logic.
experience.overview: A music app where people back artists they discover early.

experience.summary: I wrote computer science questions and reviewed model answers at Handshake AI Solutions. The work involved checking technical correctness, finding missing edge cases, and explaining why an answer was wrong.
highlights: Wrote more than 50 computer science prompts and reviewed more than 100 model answers for technical correctness, edge cases, and code errors.
experience.overview: Computer science tasks for testing and reviewing language models.

experience.summary: During my AWS internship, I built a data pipeline for assessing Kinesis stream migrations. It replaced a manual process that took more than three hours with data that the team could query in Athena.
highlights: Built AWS Glue jobs in Scala and PySpark to turn JSON and DynamoDB exports into partitioned Parquet on S3. Reduced data preparation time by about 95%.
Moved prototypes into Scala, fixed crawler timing and job-bookmark issues, and adjusted compute settings to cut runtime by 50%.
Set up infrastructure with AWS CDK and CloudFormation. Added CloudWatch alerts and dashboards for more than 100 active streams.
Compared storage and processing options and wrote design documents covering costs, schemas, and partitioning.
experience.overview: Data pipelines and migration tools for the Kinesis team.

experience.summary: At o9 Solutions, I worked on the JavaScript frontend and C# backend of an enterprise planning platform. My work covered dashboard configuration, versioning, and the tools teams used to merge changes between tenant environments.
highlights: Built configuration screens for visualization widgets so consultants could set up dashboards without writing custom code.
Developed Git-style versioning and conflict resolution for tenant configurations used by more than 20 teams.
Refactored Jasmine tests and the code they covered, removing more than 10,000 lines of duplicate code. Fixed frontend and backend bugs across releases.
experience.overview: Dashboard tools, configuration versioning, and test maintenance.

experience.summary: I built a network topology simulator at OpenNets. Engineers could configure networks in a browser, run simulations, and check settings before using them in deployment scenarios.
highlights: Used Mininet, Node.js, and MongoDB to model and validate more than 10 network topologies.
Built an AngularJS interface for editing settings and viewing network layouts.
Added automated configuration checks to catch errors before running a simulation.
experience.overview: A network simulator and the interface for configuring it.

projects.name: FluidFill
projects.summary: FluidFill turns Word templates into forms. Upload a document, fill in the detected fields, and download a completed copy with the original formatting.
highlights: Built a Next.js form editor and Python services that detect placeholders and generate document previews.
Used Gemini to identify fields, with a parser fallback when the model is unavailable. Kept repeated fields in sync and saved form answers in PostgreSQL.
projects.overview: Fill out a document once, even when the same field appears in several places.

projects.name: Realtime Study Rooms
projects.summary: I built this study-room app and a tutorial for a software engineering course. People can join rooms, chat, see who's online, and make video calls in the browser.
highlights: Built a Node.js WebSocket server for rooms, messages, and the connection setup needed for WebRTC video calls.
Wrote React hooks for connection management and media streams, plus an 11-step tutorial and starter code for other students.
projects.overview: Study rooms with chat, online status, and video calls.

projects.name: Clozyt
projects.summary: Clozyt lets people browse clothes by swiping: right to like, left to skip, and up for details. Their choices help decide what appears next.
highlights: Built the shopping interface with Next.js and Tailwind CSS, including a cart and checkout flow.
Used FashionCLIP and Qdrant to find similar products, mixed in new suggestions, and built APIs that record feedback and return the next batch of items.
projects.overview: A shopping app that learns from the clothes you like and skip.

projects.name: FluxRate
projects.summary: FluxRate is a Java simulation of a parking lot. It models entry and exit gates, tracks occupancy, and changes hourly prices as the lot fills up.
highlights: Implemented gate states, timing checks, emergency handling, and payment checks for exiting vehicles.
Ran a 24-hour scenario with 50 spaces and used Python plots to check occupancy, billing, gate behavior, and price changes.
projects.overview: A parking simulation with gate controls and prices that change with demand.

projects.name: Market Risk Forecasting Dashboard
projects.summary: I built a Python project to study market volatility and drawdown risk. It prepares historical price data, trains LSTM models, and compares their predictions with statistical baselines.
highlights: Processed historical price and trading-volume data with Python and SQL, including rolling volatility, moving averages, and correlations.
Trained TensorFlow models and deployed an inference workflow on AWS SageMaker.
projects.overview: Experiments in forecasting market volatility from historical price data.

projects.name: WhatsApp Group Chat Analysis
projects.summary: This Python project parses WhatsApp exports so you can look at activity over time, common words, and sentiment across a conversation.
highlights: Parsed more than 10,000 messages with Python, Pandas, and NumPy.
Cleaned message text with NLTK and used scikit-learn to examine sentiment and conversation patterns.
projects.overview: Explore message activity and sentiment in exported group chats.

projects.name: Handwritten Script Clustering
projects.summary: I built a tool for organizing handwritten script images into similar groups. It uses clustering to help sort a collection before further review or processing.
highlights: Used PCA to reduce image features and KMeans to group similar samples.
Compared the resulting groups and plotted them with Matplotlib to inspect how well they separated.
projects.overview: Group images of handwriting by visual similarity.

projects.name: Image Restoration with MPRNet
projects.summary: I worked with MPRNet to restore degraded natural images and compare the results with the original inputs.
highlights: Built an image-restoration workflow around a neural network model.
Compared restored images with baseline results using visual checks and peak signal-to-noise ratio.
projects.overview: Experiments in restoring noisy or damaged images.

projects.name: Senti Chat
projects.summary: Senti Chat adds sentiment labels to a live conversation. I built the React interface and connected it to an Express backend and a Python text-analysis service.
highlights: Used Pusher to deliver new messages and NLTK to process text and score sentiment.
Added tests with Jest and React Testing Library for the chat interface and its behavior.
projects.overview: A chat app that labels the sentiment of incoming messages.

projects.name: Crypto Notes
projects.summary: I built a notes app that uses wallet authentication and smart contracts to decide who can access a note. The interface uses React and Next.js, with note storage on IPFS.
highlights: Wrote Solidity contracts and used Hardhat and Ethers.js for local development and wallet interaction.
Added tests for access rules and note operations, and a GraphQL API for querying stored data.
projects.overview: A notes app with access controlled by an Ethereum wallet.

projects.name: Safe Python Execution Service
projects.summary: This Flask service runs submitted Python code in an isolated process and returns the output as JSON. I used nsjail and Docker to restrict access to the host.
highlights: Disabled network access and set limits on execution time and system resources.
Packaged the service for Google Cloud Run so it can stop when no requests are running.
projects.overview: Run submitted Python code with limits on what it can do.

projects.name: HAAS
projects.summary: I worked on HAAS, a logic-based programming language. The project covers reading source code, parsing expressions, evaluating programs, and showing results in an interactive prompt.
highlights: Implemented arithmetic, logic, control flow, and ternary expressions with Prolog grammar rules and compiler tools.
Added sample programs and tutorials to explain the language and help others run it.
projects.overview: A small programming language with a parser, evaluator, and interactive prompt.

projects.name: Pokemon Game Engine
projects.summary: I built a battle simulator in C++ with separate components for creatures, abilities, and game rules. The structure lets new creatures and moves be added without rewriting the battle loop.
highlights: Used object-oriented design and custom data structures to represent game state.
Ran simulated battles to check interactions between moves, abilities, and battle rules.
projects.overview: A C++ simulator for Pokemon battles.

projects.name: Agile Project Management App
projects.summary: I built a Java app for Planning Poker sessions. Team members can compare estimates, discuss differences, and record their decisions for later planning.
highlights: Implemented the estimation flow and the data structures for tracking tasks and votes.
Used Maven to build the app and keep the project dependencies organized.
projects.overview: Planning Poker and task estimates for software teams.

achievements.title: Built and launched TappedIn
achievements.summary: Co-founded TappedIn and built its app and backend. Now on the App Store with over 1,000 users.

achievements.title: Visual AI Hackathon Winner
achievements.summary: Won with the Food Sage team at ASU. We built an app that scans food labels, extracts ingredients, and flags potential ingredient risks.

achievements.title: 2× Performer of the Quarter
achievements.summary: Awarded Performer of the Quarter twice at o9 Solutions.

professionalSummary: Software engineer with 3+ years of experience building web and mobile apps, backend services, and data pipelines. Background in Python, TypeScript, C#, SQL, cloud infrastructure, and machine learning, with an M.S. in Software Engineering from Arizona State University.
